title: Mount Vesuvius erupts, burying Pompeii and Herculaneum
blurb: The eruption preserved Roman cities under volcanic ash for nearly 1,700 years.

title: Charlemagne is crowned Emperor of the Romans
blurb: Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne in St. Peter's Basilica on Christmas Day.

title: Battle of Hastings: William the Conqueror defeats King Harold II
blurb: The Norman victory ended Anglo-Saxon rule of England.

title: King John seals the Magna Carta at Runnymede
blurb: The charter limited royal power and seeded the principle of rule of law.

title: Constantinople falls to Sultan Mehmed II's Ottoman forces
blurb: The fall of the Byzantine capital is often used to mark the end of the Middle Ages.

title: Johannes Gutenberg prints the Gutenberg Bible in Mainz
blurb: The first major book printed using movable type in Europe.

title: Christopher Columbus's expedition makes landfall in the Bahamas
blurb: The voyage opened sustained European contact with the Americas.

title: Jamestown, the first permanent English settlement in North America, is founded
blurb: Settlers of the Virginia Company established the colony along the James River.

title: Isaac Newton publishes Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica
blurb: The work laid out classical mechanics and the law of universal gravitation.

title: A massive earthquake and tsunami devastate Lisbon
blurb: The disaster killed tens of thousands and shaped Enlightenment thinking.

title: James Hargreaves invents the spinning jenny
blurb: The multi-spool spinning frame was a key early invention of the Industrial Revolution.

title: The Continental Congress adopts the Declaration of Independence
blurb: Thirteen American colonies declared themselves independent of Great Britain.

title: The Bastille is stormed in Paris, igniting the French Revolution
blurb: Parisians attacked the medieval fortress in search of arms and political prisoners.

title: Napoleon is defeated at the Battle of Waterloo
blurb: Coalition forces under Wellington and Blücher ended Napoleonic rule of France.

title: The Erie Canal opens, linking the Great Lakes to the Atlantic
blurb: The canal transformed New York into the principal commercial port of the U.S.

title: The Indian Rebellion against the British East India Company begins
blurb: The uprising at Meerut led the Crown to take direct control of India.

title: Charles Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species
blurb: The book introduced the theory of evolution by natural selection to a wide public.

title: Abraham Lincoln issues the Emancipation Proclamation
blurb: The proclamation declared enslaved people in Confederate states to be free.

title: The First Transcontinental Railroad is completed at Promontory Summit
blurb: Railroad workers drove the golden spike linking the Atlantic and Pacific by rail.

title: Alexander Graham Bell is granted a patent for the telephone
blurb: The patent kicked off rapid commercial deployment of telephone networks.

title: Thomas Edison demonstrates a long-lasting incandescent light bulb
blurb: The carbon-filament lamp burned for over 13 hours in his Menlo Park lab.

title: The Statue of Liberty is dedicated in New York Harbor
blurb: A gift from France, the statue became an icon of immigration to the United States.

title: The Wright brothers achieve the first powered, controlled airplane flight
blurb: Orville flew the Wright Flyer 120 feet at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.

title: The RMS Titanic strikes an iceberg and sinks in the North Atlantic
blurb: More than 1,500 people died on the ship's maiden voyage.

title: Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria is assassinated in Sarajevo
blurb: The killing triggered the chain of events that led to World War I.

title: Alexander Fleming discovers penicillin
blurb: The accidental discovery launched the era of antibiotic medicine.

title: Japan attacks the U.S. naval base at Pearl Harbor
blurb: The surprise attack brought the United States into World War II.

title: Allied forces land in Normandy on D-Day
blurb: The largest seaborne invasion in history opened the Western Front in WWII.

title: Xerox introduces the 914, the first successful plain-paper photocopier
blurb: The machine made document copying cheap and ubiquitous in offices.

title: Apollo 11 astronauts land on the Moon
blurb: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans to walk on the lunar surface.

title: Reactor No. 4 at the Chernobyl nuclear plant explodes
blurb: The accident released radioactive contamination across much of Europe.

title: Tim Berners-Lee circulates his proposal for the World Wide Web at CERN
blurb: The memo "Information Management: A Proposal" outlined what became the web.

title: The Berlin Wall is opened, ending decades of division
blurb: East Germany's announcement of free travel led crowds to dismantle the wall overnight.

title: Coordinated terrorist attacks strike the World Trade Center and the Pentagon
blurb: Nearly 3,000 people died and the attacks reshaped global security policy.

title: Steve Jobs unveils the first iPhone at Macworld
blurb: The device combined a phone, iPod, and internet communicator into one product.

title: Barack Obama is elected the 44th President of the United States
blurb: Obama became the first Black president in U.S. history.

title: The World Health Organization declares COVID-19 a pandemic
blurb: The declaration came as cases spread across more than 100 countries.
